LESSON: HOLDING TOOLS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Tools and Production
Topic 4.1: Holding tools
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Holding tools, part of Tools and Production in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why are holding tools necessary in a workplace? 2. How are holding tools used in a workshop?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: A learner develops listening and speaking skills when discussing the use of holding tools.

• Learning to learn: A learner acquires reflection skills when demonstrating safe use of holding tools to perform given tasks.

• Digital Literacy: A learner develops interacting skills when manipulating audio visual aids on safe use of holding tools.

Values:
• Unity: A learner co-operates with others during discussions on the safe use of holding tools.

• Responsibility: A learner exercises accountability as they maintain and store holding tools.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• Agriculture and Nutrition: A learner identifies and demonstrates how to use and care for holding tools.

• Integrated Science: A learner uses simple machines to perform different tasks.

Suggested Learning Resources:

• Holding tools(pliers, clamps, tongs and clips).

• Tactile audio-visual aids or audio-video aids.

• Digital device with assistive technology.

• Print and Braille Pre-Technical Studies.
